findings.title: Unsafe dict access can crash the install pipeline instead of failing gracefully
findings.body: The new user-mismatch check does `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` using direct dict indexing instead of `.get()`. If an existing `Integration` row (reached via the 'OrganizationIntegration does not exist, but Integration does exist' branch, e.g. a re-install of a previously uninstalled/legacy integration, or one created without full sender data) has a `metadata` dict that lacks the `sender` key or the `sender` dict lacks `login`, this raises an unhandled `KeyError`. That turns what should be a controlled 'Invalid installation request.' error page into an uncaught 500, which directly contradicts the goal of this PR (gracefully rejecting mismatched installs). This should use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and compare, falling back to the error response when missing.

findings.title: Unhandled exception from get_user_info() on GitHub API failure
findings.body: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the call `authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is not wrapped in a try/except, unlike the token-exchange response parsing just above it (which explicitly catches `Exception` when decoding/parsing the token response). If GitHub's `/user` endpoint returns an error (rate limiting, network failure, invalid/expired token edge cases, etc.), `get_user_info` can raise (e.g. `ApiError`), which will propagate out of the pipeline view as an unhandled exception and produce a generic 500 error instead of the intended friendly 'github-integration-failed.html' error page that the rest of this flow is designed to show.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the scenario it is named for
findings.body: `test_installation_not_found` stubs a 404 response for `/app/installations/{installation_id}` to simulate GitHub reporting that the app installation cannot be found (originally asserting 'The GitHub installation could not be found.'). After this change, the second request uses `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, which does not match `pipeline.signature` (the correct value used elsewhere in these tests is `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`). Because `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` checks `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` and returns the generic error immediately on mismatch, the request never reaches the code path that calls `get_installation_info`/`build_integration`, so the stubbed 404 response is never exercised. The test now only verifies the unrelated 'state mismatch' error path while the mocked 404 scenario (and its original purpose) goes untested, and the test's name/setup is misleading about what it actually checks.
